newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Troops start Chechnya pullout, but problems remain.
newsitem.headline: Troops start Chechnya pullout, but problems remain.

text.p: Russian troops began pulling out of Chechnya on Sunday under a peace deal signed with the rebels last month but still in doubt.
A military band struck up cheerful music at a farewell ceremony at the Russian military airport outside the Chechen capital Grozny where the 133rd battalion began the withdrawal.

The overall commander of troops Vyacheslav Tikhomirov thanked the soldiers, wished them well and handed out medals in a low-key ceremony reflecting mixed feelings over the withdrawal after 21 months of bloody and inconclusive fighting.
"For your service, for military achievements, all the best to you and a safe journey home," Tikhomirov said, to the sound of polite clapping from the rows of conscripts.

Russian television showed wrecked armoured vehicles alongside the tanks lined up on a muddy field east of Grozny, shattered at the beginning of the conflict in early 1995 and again last month before Moscow signed a truce with the rebels.
Itar-Tass news agency said the battalion had taken part in all major battles in the breakaway region and had a fearsome reputation among the separatists, who nicknamed it "black wing".
Wrecked armoured vehicles alongside the rows of tanks lined up on the muddy field testified to the ferocity of the fighting, in which tens of thousands of people have been killed.

The peace deal, signed last month after Moscow was humiliated by a rebel attack on Grozny, provides for the withdrawal of all Russian troops temporarily stationed in the region. But there is disagreement about what that involves.

The rebels say the fact that there were no troops in Chechnya before the conflict began in late 1994 means that all of them must pull out. But the Russian side has said that some troops will be based there permanently.

President Boris Yeltsin added to the confusion on Thursday when he broke his silence on his envoy Alexander Lebed's peace mission by saying he backed the deal but opposed the early withdrawal of troops.
Tikhomirov said the deal Lebed signed with the rebels was the last chance for the conflict to be resolved peacefully.

"Today's attempt at a peaceful resolution of the military conflict in Chechnya is already the third. There will not be a fourth," Tass quoted him as telling reporters. "If this attempt fails, the issue will be resolved with other methods and means."

Interfax news agency quoted Tikhomirov as saying that Lebed, Yeltsin's national security adviser and secretary of his Security Council, might return to Chechnya on Tuesday to discuss outstanding problems with the deal.
"In the last few days quite a few questions and problems have built up which demand the direct participation of the Security Council Secretary," it quoted him as saying.

"Pray God that this time it's really peace and not another case of giving up ground," Tikhomirov said. The military have complained that previous ceasefires only helped the rebels rearm and regain positions won through months of combat.
Fighting has died right down since the August 21 ceasefire but military officials told Tass on Sunday that one soldier had been killed and one wounded when their positions were fired on.
The latest deal has fuelled hopes for a lasting peace because it has tackled the issue at the heart of the conflict for the first time -- the region's political status.
But it involves an uneasy compromise -- postponing any decision on the issue for five years -- and is vague on detail.
Critics have warned that the rebels -- whose former leader declared Chechnya independent in 1991 -- may use it to take power, invalidating the Russian military campaign.

Tass quoted sources close to the talks Lebed held with rebel chief-of-staff Aslan Maskhadov as saying that Maskhadov had welcomed the departure of the 133rd battalion, which is due to return to its base near St Petersburg.
"That battalion is a pain in the neck, let it be the first to go," the sources quoted Maskhadov as saying.
